prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for all Houston residents — the best choice depends on your neighborhood, whether it’s residential vs. commercial, how quickly you need service, and your budget. I can, however, help you find a top option and tell you what to look for.

If you want a quick recommendation tailored to you, tell me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and whether this is an emergency, and I’ll list the highest-rated local HVAC companies and recent review notes.

How to pick the best Houston AC repair company
- License & insurance: Verify the contractor is licensed in Texas (TDLR) and carries liability insurance. Ask for license number and proof of insurance.  
- Local reviews & reputation: Check Google, Yelp, and BBB for recent reviews and response to complaints. Look for consistently high ratings and longevity in the market.  
- Experience with your system: Make sure they service your brand/model (especially if you have a heat pump, packaged unit, or an older system).  
- Transparent pricing: Get a written estimate that separates diagnostic fee, parts, labor, and refrigerant (if needed). Ask if they charge flat-rate or time-and-materials.  
- Warranties: Ask about warranties on parts and labor and whether they honor manufacturer warranties.  
- Availability & response time: Ask about emergency/after-hours service, typical arrival window, and any diagnostic fee credits if you proceed with repair.  
- Maintenance plans: If you want long-term reliability, ask about tune-up plans that include priority service and discounts.  
- Technician credentials: Ask if technicians are NATE-certified (a good indicator of training).

Common red flags
- No license or unwillingness to provide it.  
- Very low bids far below competitors (could mean inferior parts or cutting corners).  
- High-pressure sales or pushing for complete replacement before diagnostic proof.  
- No written estimate or vague warranty terms.

Typical cost ranges (Houston, approximate)
- Diagnostic/service call: $75–$150 (varies).  
- Simple repairs (capacitor, contactor): $100–$400.  
- Refrigerant recharge: $150–$400 (depends on refrigerant type).  
- Major components (compressor, coil): $1,000–$4,000+.  
(Prices vary — get written estimates.)

Well-regarded national/local options you might consider checking (verify local reviews and licenses):
- Local independent companies with long Houston presence often have the best local reputation — I can pull current top choices for your ZIP.  
- National brands with Houston locations you can check: One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning; Service Experts; Aire Serv; ARS/Rescue Rooter. (Local franchise quality varies — read local reviews.)

Next step
If you tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and whether it’s an urgent repair, I’ll gather the top-rated local AC repair companies and summarize their average ratings, hours, emergency service, and what customers say.
